newsitem.title: USA: N.J. fiscal '97 year-to-date revenues at $14.4 bln.
newsitem.headline: N.J. fiscal '97 year-to-date revenues at $14.4 bln.

text.p: New Jersey Treasurer Brian Clymer said Wednesday the state collected $14.4 billion of revenues during the first 11 months of fiscal 1997, or 1.4 percent more than revised projections.
For the month of May, revenue collections were $1.2 billion, which was 2.9 percent over expectations, the treasurer said in a statement.
The gross income tax and the corporation business tax significantly outpaced expectations, Clymer said. But revenues from the state lottery trailed projections.

The gross income tax generated $4.4 billion, or $147.1 million above forecast, and corporate business taxes totaled more than $1.1 billion for the eleven-month period ending May 31. That figure included $129 of unexpected revenues.
Lottery collections were $25 million below expectations, at $577 million.
